title: System requirements
content:
Before you start using Innopolis VM, make sure your device and network meet these requirements.
Browser# You access Innopolis VM through a web browser. Use one of these (or any that work with the same standards):
Browser Minimum version Google Chrome 120+ Mozilla Firefox 120+ Microsoft Edge 120+ Safari 17+ Older versions may not display the dashboard correctly.
Network# Internet connection: Stable broadband (at least 5 Mbps download). Ports: Outbound connections to ports 22 (SSH) and 443 (HTTPS) must be open. SSO access: You must be able to reach sso.university.innopolis.ru for login. If you work from a university campus network, these ports are open by default. If you work from home and use a corporate VPN, check with your IT team.
Hardware (for web console access)# If you connect to your VM through the browser (WebConsole), your device needs:
RAM: 4 GB minimum, 8 GB recommended. Screen resolution: 1280×720 or higher. JavaScript: Enabled in your browser. Hardware (for SSH clients)# If you connect via PuTTY, MobaXterm, or another SSH client:
OS: Windows 10/11, macOS 12+, or Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+). SSH client installed: PuTTY (Windows), MobaXterm (Windows/Linux/macOS), or built-in ssh command (macOS/Linux). Account# You need an active Innopolis University account with access to Innopolis VM. If you cannot log in, contact your instructor or the IT support team.
Once your device and account meet these requirements, you can get access to Innopolis VM and create your first subscription.

title: How to visit Innopolis VM
content: How to visit Innopolis VM# Open your web browser and type Innopolis VM in the address bar. Then you will be redirected to the SSO Innopolis University login page. If you see the main page immediately, you are already logged in. If you are not logged in, you will be prompted to enter your Innopolis University credentials (username and password). Then click on the Sign in button. You will be redirected to the main page of the website.

title: Setup
content: Before you can create virtual machines, you need to get access to Innopolis VM and create a subscription.

content: Learn how to create virtual machines (VMs) from scratch or from pre-configured templates.

title: Password requirements
content:
When you create a virtual machine (VM), you set a password for the administrator account. Follow these rules to avoid creation errors.
Rules# Requirement Value Minimum length 12 characters Maximum length 128 characters Uppercase letters At least 1 (A–Z) Lowercase letters At least 1 (a–z) Numbers At least 1 (0–9) Special characters At least 1 (`!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{} Examples# Password Result Why MyStrongPass2026! ✅ Accepted Meets all rules short1A! ❌ Rejected Too short (8 characters, need 12) alllowercase123! ❌ Rejected No uppercase letter NoNumbersHere! ❌ Rejected No digit Related pages:

title: Subscriptions
content: How to create a subscription# From the main page of the website, click on the NEW button in the left bottom corner. The new menu will open - click MY ACCOUNT. Click on the ADD SUBSCRIPTION button. Modal with subscription creation form will open. Depending on who you are (student, instructor, worker), you will have different options for subscription creation. For example, for students, you can create a subscription for a specific course or general StudentPublic subscription. If you want a specific subscription, you need to contact IT department of Innopolis University. The details of the concrete subscription type will appear on the right side of the form when you click it. When you choose the subscription type - click it and then click the tick button on the right bottom corner. Then you need to wait while the subscription is being created. Some time your subscription will have the “Syncing” status. Don’t worry, just wait until it will be “Active”. After a while, your subscription will change its status to “Active”. Where to find your subscriptions# From the main page of the website, click on the My Account button in the left bar. Click on the SUBSCRIPTIONS section. You can see all your subscriptions.

title: Create a virtual machine (VM)
content: How to create a new VM# At first, you need to have a subscription to the service (see Subscriptions). From the main page of the website, click on the VIRTUAL MACHINES button in the left bar. On the Virtual Machines page, click on the right arrow button OR if you have already created some VMs, click on the NEW button in the left bottom corner and then STANDALONE VIRTUAL MACHINE. In the opened menu, choose one of two creation methods: FROM GALLERY: Detailed configuration with pre-configured templates. Best for specific requirements. (see How to create a new virtual machine from gallery) Quick Start: Fast creation with basic settings. Best for simple VMs. (sese How to create a new virtual machine via QUICK CREATE)

title: Functions
content: Once your virtual machine (VM) is running, you can connect to it, view details, and manage settings.

title: Glossary
content:
This glossary defines the key terms used in the Innopolis virtual machine (VM) documentation.
A# Administrator account The default user account on a VM. It has full control over the system. On Linux VMs, this is usually the root user. On Windows VMs, it is the Administrator user.
D# Dashboard The main web page where you manage your virtual machines and subscriptions. You open it after logging in to Innopolis VM.
G# Gallery A catalog of pre-configured VM templates. Each template includes an operating system and, in some cases, pre-installed software.
I# Innopolis VM The service that lets students, instructors, and staff of Innopolis University create and manage virtual machines.
IP address A number that identifies your VM on the network. It looks like 10.13.127.89. You need the IP address to connect to your VM via SSH.
S# SSH key A pair of files (public and private) that you use to connect to a VM securely, without a password. The public key is stored on the VM. The private key stays on your device.
SSH client A program that lets you connect to a VM over the SSH protocol. Examples: PuTTY, MobaXterm, or the built-in ssh command in macOS and Linux.
Subscription An access plan that defines your resource limits (CPU, RAM, storage) within Innopolis VM. You need an active subscription to create a VM.
T# Template A ready-made configuration for a VM. A template includes the operating system and, sometimes, pre-installed software. You choose a template when you create a VM from the gallery.
V# VM Virtual machine. A software-based emulation of a physical computer. After the first mention in a text, we use the abbreviation “VM”.
VM details The page that shows information about a specific VM: its status, IP address, operating system, and creation date.
WebConsole A browser-based interface that lets you connect to your VM without installing an SSH client. You open it from the VM dashboard by clicking CONNECT and then WebConsole.
Did not find the term you need? Check the System requirements page or the Troubleshooting section.

title: Create a virtual machine (VM) from gallery
content:
You chose the FROM GALLERY creation method. This option allows you to configure a VM in detail using pre-configured templates.
How to create a new VM from gallery# Menu with gallery creating will open. You can choose the different operating system for your VM and see the details. When you have chosen, click the right arrow button. Menu with settings of your VM will open. Now you need to write the name of your VM into NAME field. Name is required. Write and confirm the new password for your VM. If you see the red exclamation mark in the PASSWORD field then the condition on the password is not satisfied (see Password requirements). If you see the red exclamation mark in the CONFIRM field then the password and confirm password are not equal. ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT may be filled by default and can’t be changed. But in some cases you are required to write your own name inside the field. Also you can write your ssh key into the SSH KEY field or product key into the PRODUCT KEY field. This is not required. Save your password, administrator account and ssh key or product key, because you will not be able to see them again. When you have filled all fields, click the right arrow button. Then you can set your VM network adapter - where your VM be available. Now you can click the tick button to save your settings and create VM.

title: Connect to a virtual machine (VM)
content:
How to connect to your VM# You have three options to connect to your VM:
SSH client — Use PuTTY (Windows) or MobaXterm (Windows, Linux, macOS). Requires an SSH key configured during VM creation. Browser — Connect directly from your web browser (see How to connect to your VM from the browser). SSH by IP — Connect using the VM’s IP address with any SSH client (see How to see the IP of the VM). How to see the IP of the VM# On your VM dashboard, find the IP address on the right side of the page. The IP looks like this: 10.13.127.89. If there is no IP, see the section “How to create a VM with an explicit IP” (will be updated soon). How to connect to your VM from the browser# On your VM dashboard, click the CONNECT button at the bottom. Choose the connection method. To connect from the browser, click WebConsole. A new browser window will open with your VM console. Enter your VM login (see What is my VM login) and press Enter. Enter your VM password and press Enter. If you see the message Login is incorrect, you entered the wrong login or password. Try again with the correct credentials. If you successfully connected, you will see a message like Welcome to Ubuntu… or similar, depending on your VM operating system.

title: Create a virtual machine (VM) via Quick Create
content:
You chose the QUICK CREATE method. This option allows you to quickly create a VM with basic settings.
How to create a new VM via QUICK CREATE# Menu with quick start creating will open. Here you need to write the name of your VM into NAME field. Name is required. Also choose the subscription type - depending on it you can choose different templates (operating systems) for VM. Then choose the template (operating system) for your VM. Write and confirm the new password for your VM. If you see the red exclamation mark in the PASSWORD field then the condition on the password is not satisfied (see Password requirements). ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT may be filled by default and can’t be changed. But in some cases you are required to write your own name inside the field. Save your password, administrator account and ssh key or product key, because you will not be able to see them again. If all fields are filled correctly - click the CREATE VM INSTANCE button. To see the details of creation - click on the DETAILS button. You can see the progress of creation of your VM here. On the VMs page you can see your VM. For some time its status will be “Creating”, then it will change to “Running”.

title: Details & credentials
content: How to see details of the created virtual machine (VM)# From the main page of the website, click on the VIRTUAL MACHINES button in the left bar. Choose the VM you want to see the details of and click on its NAME. Then you can see the page with your VM. If you want to see details, click DASHBOARD button. Then you can see the page with your VM dashboard. What is my VM login# The VM login is not displayed after creation. The default login is usually root, admin, or administrator. You can see the login of your VM during VM creation. For QUICK START option, you can see the login in the ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT section. The login is most likely lower-case instead of upper-case. Or you are required to fulfill it. For FROM GALLERY option, you can see the login in the ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT section.

title: Troubleshooting
content:
Troubleshooting# This section helps you diagnose and resolve common issues with Innopolis VM. Each problem follows a structured approach: Symptom, Possible causes, Checks, Solutions, and Escalation.
Gray screen — cannot click anything# Symptom:
The screen turned gray and you cannot interact with the interface.
Possible causes:
Your session has timed out due to inactivity. The browser lost connection to the server. The browser tab is unresponsive. Checks:
Look at the bottom of the screen for a message like «Your session timed out. Click OK to log in again». Check your internet connection. Solutions:
Click OK in the message. Log in again with your Innopolis University credentials. If the message does not appear, refresh the browser page. Escalation:
If the problem persists after refreshing and logging in again, contact the IT department of Innopolis University.
Subscription is syncing for too long# Symptom:
Your subscription has been in the «Syncing» status for more than 10 minutes.
Possible causes:
Normal synchronization delay with the SSO system. Temporary server-side processing. An issue with your account permissions. Checks:
Check the current status of your subscription on the My Account → SUBSCRIPTIONS page. Try to create a VM — if it works, the subscription is already active despite the «Syncing» label. Solutions:
Wait 10–15 minutes. In most cases, the status will change to «Active» automatically. Try using the subscription — it is likely already active. Escalation:
If the subscription remains in «Syncing» status for more than 30 minutes, contact the IT department of Innopolis University.
VM is creating for too long# Symptom:
Your VM has been in the «Creating» status for more than 15 minutes.
Possible causes:
High load on the Innopolis VM servers. Insufficient resources in your subscription. A template configuration error. Checks:
Check the VM status on the VIRTUAL MACHINES page. Wait at least 15 minutes — some templates take longer to provision. Solutions:
Delete the stuck VM. Create a new VM with the same settings. Escalation:
If you have tried to recreate the VM 2–3 times and it still fails, contact the IT department of Innopolis University.
VM failed to create# Symptom:
You received an error message during VM creation.
Possible causes:
Incorrect password (does not meet requirements). Insufficient resources in your subscription. A template or configuration error. Checks:
Click the i button next to the failed VM to see the error details. Review the error message for specific clues. Solutions:
Fix the issue described in the error message (e.g., change the password to meet requirements). Delete the failed VM and create a new one with corrected settings. Escalation:
If the error persists after 2–3 attempts with corrected settings, contact the IT department of Innopolis University.
Forgot account password# Symptom:
You cannot log in to Innopolis VM with your Innopolis University credentials.
Possible causes:
You forgot your password. Incorrect keyboard layout or Caps Lock is on. Your account is locked or deactivated. Checks:
Verify your keyboard layout and make sure Caps Lock is off. Try logging in at sso.university.innopolis.ru directly. Solutions:
Use the «Forgot password» option on the SSO login page to reset your password. Log in again with the new password. Escalation:
If you cannot reset your password or your account is locked, contact the IT department of Innopolis University.
Forgot VM password# Symptom:
You cannot log in to your VM via SSH or WebConsole.
Possible causes:
You forgot the password you set during VM creation. Incorrect keyboard layout or Caps Lock is on. The password was changed by another administrator. Checks:
Verify your keyboard layout and make sure Caps Lock is off. Try the default logins: root, admin, or administrator (depending on the OS). Check if you still have an active WebConsole session. Solutions:
Warning: Recreating a VM permanently deletes all data on it. Back up your files before proceeding.
If you cannot recover the password, you have two options:
Use the WebConsole if you still have an active session — you can change the password from inside the VM. Recreate the VM with a new password. Escalation:
If you need to recover data from a VM with a lost password, contact the IT department of Innopolis University immediately — they may be able to help before the VM is deleted.
